- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the low-end of the range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to underestimate true price during early part of 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward bias by +1–2% for days 1–7.  
- Overshoots after strong sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.0) are common — cap forecast at 10% below the immediate prior peak.  
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if 10-day average of true prices is lower than forecast, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0 → 0.8), model overreacts to the first swing — dampen forecast response to the second swing by 10–15%.
